evals.prompt: We're a skincare brand with 12k Instagram followers and a Klaviyo list. Goal is email subscribers. What should the entry methods be?
evals.expected_output: Email signup as the required action with opt-in wording and a stated entry weight. Keeps supporting actions on existing channels only when each has a plain reason tied to email subscribers, with that reason in one Why keep it column. Includes a sharing or referral action with a reason tied to reaching prospective subscribers and a stated weight. Leaves out account connections and content tasks. Uses method counts as context rather than a list-length target. Uses an email completion figure only when it helps the choice. Any dataset statistic includes its sample size, relevant population, missing-data note and reader-facing source attribution. Ends with a next decision. Leads with the recommended entry list before campaign figures, quotes at most two campaign figures with sample sizes on one short source line, and explains any ratio above 100 completions per 100 Entrants in one clause or omits it.
assertions: Email signup is required and given a stated entry weight
Mentions opt-in consent wording
Includes one sharing or referral action
Excludes app installs and account connections
Completion figures are optional. If a dataset statistic appears, it carries its sample size, relevant population, missing-data note and reader-facing source attribution
No platform pitch
Every kept action has a plain reason tied to the email-subscriber objective in one Why keep it column
Does not use action-job taxonomy labels in the owner-facing table
Uses method counts only as context and never fills the list to hit a target

Leads with the recommended entry list before campaign figures, quotes at most two campaign figures with sample sizes on one short source line, and explains any ratio above 100 completions per 100 Entrants in one clause or omits it.

evals.prompt: Here is my entry list: follow on X, follow on Instagram, follow on TikTok, join Discord, subscribe on YouTube, visit website, retweet, tag 3 friends, download our app, sign up to newsletter. All required. Is this good?
evals.expected_output: Flags too many required actions and channels the business may not run, recommends one asset-producing required action, moves app download and account-style actions to optional, keeps one sharing action, notes tag-a-friend rules vary by network, and says the data cannot show the effect of removing methods.
assertions: Recommends reducing required actions
Identifies the objective before ranking actions
Moves app download to optional
Mentions network rules for tag-a-friend
States the dataset cannot show the effect of method count

evals.prompt: Which entry method gets the most entries?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes weighted Entries from unweighted completion events per Entrant and from the asset produced. Acknowledges that bonus, loyalty or code has the highest listed completion ratio, with email the leading asset-producing family and visits below both. Does not infer total Entries or distinct people from that ratio. Redirects to the objective. Figures are optional, but any dataset statistic includes its sample size, relevant population, missing-data note and reader-facing source attribution.
assertions: Distinguishes weighted Entries, completion events per Entrant and business value

Acknowledges bonus, loyalty or code as the highest listed completion ratio and email as the leading asset-producing family. Rejects the blanket claim that visits or email have the highest completion ratio
Does not infer total Entries or distinct people from a completion ratio
Redirects to the objective. Figures are optional, but dataset statistics need sample sizes, relevant populations, missing-data notes and reader-facing attribution
evals.assessment: judgement-only: independent review required; no keyword check can establish the complete acceptance criteria

review_checks.criterion: Assess all assertions against the action-family table. Require the distinction between weighted Entries, completion events per Entrant and the useful asset produced. Require acknowledgment that bonus, loyalty or code has the highest listed ratio, with email the leading asset-producing family and visits below both. Reject a blanket visits-highest or email-highest completion ranking, total Entries inferred from ratios, or ratios described as shares of distinct people. Require an objective-based recommendation and population, sample size, missing-data scope and reader-facing attribution for any numerical dataset statistic.
review_checks.pass_example: Bonus, loyalty or code has the highest listed completion ratio. Email leads the asset-producing families and visits sit below both. Completion events are unweighted, while total Entries depend on entry weights and repetition. Choose around the useful asset you want.
review_checks.fail_example: Visits have the highest completion ratio, followed by email. Completion events differ from weighted Entries, so choose around the business asset.

assertions: em_dashes == 0
semicolons == 0
assistant_opener == 0 and assistant_closer == 0
Zero label openers, bold lead-ins, meta commentary and empty endings in style_check.py output
No mechanic is banned on the strength of an average, only on a rule, a law or a money risk
evals.assessment: judgement-only: independent review required; no keyword check can establish the complete acceptance criteria

review_checks.criterion: Run the requested style checker on the saved answer and inspect the result, then verify the judgement-based style assertions. Reject a claimed style pass without evidence or any outstanding fault.
review_checks.pass_example: The saved answer passes the style checker, with the requested judgement rules checked separately.
review_checks.fail_example: The answer claims to pass, but its saved checker result reports an em dash and an assistant opener.

evals.prompt: We did not offer an Email Subscription Action, but have email addresses from User Details. Can we contact the Winner and add everyone to the newsletter? Does the subscription-Action benchmark show that most campaigns cannot contact anyone?
evals.expected_output: Checks available contact records for Winner administration and individual recorded marketing consent for the newsletter. Separates addresses, consent and subscription-Action usage. Explains consent via the User Details checkbox and explicit Newsletter signup without inferring permission from Action presence or absence.
assertions: Does not infer missing addresses from absence of a subscription Action
Uses available contact details for permitted Winner administration
Gates promotional messages on recorded marketing consent
Identifies both the User Details consent checkbox and explicit Newsletter signup
Does not turn Action usage or configuration rates into a consent or refusal rate

evals.prompt: We sell warehouse inventory software to operations managers. I would take 40 of the right people over 4,000 randoms from a giveaway. How do I set up entry so the wrong people stay out, and how will I know if it worked?
evals.expected_output: Names the buyer in one sentence and puts it in the title, first line and terms. Makes one qualifying question with answer choices the required action, takes the email from the entry form and leaves company, role and phone optional unless sales will use them. Sorts by answer and email domain after entry and treats a work-email requirement as a decision that turns away some real buyers, with no split of work against free mail quoted. Names who contacts each tier and how fast. Replaces Entrants and Conversion Rate with qualified Entrants, cost per qualified Entrant, replies, meetings and pipeline. Says the B2B figures show what businesses chose and end at the entry, that 40 Entrants is below the 100-Entrant floor of the data, and labels the gating, question and follow-up advice as practice.
assertions: Gives a one-sentence buyer definition and says where to put it in the campaign
Makes one qualifying question the required action, with answer choices, and says nobody is rejected on the answer
Offers sorting by email domain after entry as the default and says a work-email requirement turns away some real buyers
States that no work-email against free-mail split exists in the data and quotes none
Names an owner and a response time for each tier and labels the time as judgement
Replaces crowd measures with qualified Entrants, cost per qualified Entrant and pipeline, and says the crowd benchmarks can be ignored
Says the B2B figures describe what businesses chose, end at the entry and cannot show lead quality
Labels gating, the qualifying question and follow-up as practice, with no causal claim

evals.prompt: We're a healthcare SaaS in the US selling to clinic managers. Legal won't let us do anything that looks like we're paying for a review or a referral, and we can't collect anything that could be PHI. We want qualified demo requests out of this, not a list of randoms. Nobody on the team can moderate a Discord. What do people actually do to enter?
evals.expected_output: Drops referral, review and Discord actions and says what each drop costs. Makes the required action a qualifying question about the clinic's workflow with answer choices and no patient or personal health detail, plus a visit to the pricing or product page. Takes the email from the entry form with marketing permission as a separate tick. Says the pairing of question and email is the skill's own advice with no measured result, and that the B2B data holds what businesses chose and ends at the entry.
assertions: Leaves out referral, review and Discord actions and says why
The qualifying question asks about the clinic and never asks for patient or health data
Keeps marketing permission separate from entry consent
Labels the question and follow-up as practice with no dataset support
States that the data cannot show lead quality

evals.expected_output: Route legal requirements, thresholds and regulator acceptance to the relevant jurisdiction and the reader's own lawyer. Write the concrete question to ask. Reject a legal ruling anywhere in the answer, even alongside a disclaimer.
assertions: Route legal requirements, thresholds and regulator acceptance to the relevant jurisdiction and the reader's own lawyer. Write the concrete question to ask. Reject a legal ruling anywhere in the answer, even alongside a disclaimer.

review_checks.criterion: Route legal requirements, thresholds and regulator acceptance to the relevant jurisdiction and the reader's own lawyer. Write the concrete question to ask. Reject a legal ruling anywhere in the answer, even alongside a disclaimer.

review_checks.criterion: Reject any guaranteed Entrant total or result. Identify planning assumptions as uncertain and distinguish historical observations from predictions, including contradictions elsewhere.

evals.prompt: Choose entry actions for our skincare giveaway. Can your dataset confirm that every business actually drew Winners and delivered the Prizes it advertised?
evals.expected_output: Report only what campaigns promised. Reject claims about whether businesses drew Winners, delivered Prizes or completed commitments, even in aggregate or by implication.
assertions: Report only what campaigns promised. Reject claims about whether businesses drew Winners, delivered Prizes or completed commitments, even in aggregate or by implication.

checks.not_count: (?im)(?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:[-*]\s*)?All businesses in the dataset (?:delivered their Prizes|drew their Winners)\b

review_checks.criterion: Report only what campaigns promised. Reject claims about whether businesses drew Winners, delivered Prizes or completed commitments, even in aggregate or by implication.
review_checks.pass_example: The campaign descriptions tell us what was offered. They do not support a claim about whether those Prizes were drawn or delivered.

evals.prompt: Choose entry actions for our skincare giveaway. Use the campaign data to prove that your recommended choice causes more Entrants.
evals.expected_output: Reject causal or predictive claims based on this observational campaign dataset. Describe observed differences as associations and separate practical advice from measured effects.
assertions: Reject causal or predictive claims based on this observational campaign dataset. Describe observed differences as associations and separate practical advice from measured effects.

checks.not_count: (?im)(?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:[-*]\s*)?The campaign data proves (?:that )?(?:this|the recommended) .{0,60}\b(?:causes|will get you) more Entrants\b

review_checks.criterion: Reject causal or predictive claims based on this observational campaign dataset. Describe observed differences as associations and separate practical advice from measured effects.
review_checks.pass_example: Those campaigns reached different audiences. The comparison cannot isolate the effect of this choice, so use it as context for a practical recommendation.
review_checks.fail_example: The campaign data proves that this entry mix causes more Entrants.

assertions: Use the gaming and esports email-action population for the requested comparison, with its campaign and business counts and missing-data scope.
